question: Can these local models perform each arithmetic suboperation in the receiver task when tested directly without simulator tool orchestration?
motivation: In v0.12, preloading the correct receive transcript did not produce an exact receiver output for either model. Separate local-prefix computation, vector-offset addition, and the combined transformation before attributing failure to communication or protocol design.
task_suite: PrefixSum short-shard v0.3, paired reuse of 24 v0.11 cases; no new held-out task-family claim
design: For each Qwen model, run three direct arithmetic conditions for all 24 task cases (72 episodes/model, 144 total). No multi-agent simulator, tools, or messages are used. Alternate condition order by task index. One greedy completion per task and condition.

conditions.name: local_prefix
conditions.task: Given the Agent 1 shard x, compute p_i=sum(x_1..x_i), the local inclusive prefix vector. Return only a JSON array of integers.
conditions.expected: local inclusive prefix of Agent 1's shard

conditions.name: offset_vector
conditions.task: Given the exact precomputed local prefix vector p and correct offset s=sum(Agent 0 shard), return q_i=p_i+s for every element. Return only a JSON array of integers.
conditions.expected: Agent 1 local prefix vector shifted by the exact Agent 0 subtotal

conditions.name: combined_receiver
conditions.task: Given Agent 1 shard x and correct offset s=sum(Agent 0 shard), compute p_i=sum(x_1..x_i) and return q_i=p_i+s. Return only a JSON array of integers.

runtime: llama.cpp b11202, commit fcb3074f2, Windows x64 CUDA 12.4; RTX 4060 8 GB; 99 GPU layers requested; context 8192; temperature 0; max 128 generated tokens
warmup: One unscored 'Reply with OK' request per model, excluded from outcomes.
primary_outcomes: strict exact integer-array match by model, arithmetic condition, and length
strict JSON-array parse success separately from mathematical exactness
paired per-task changes between local_prefix, offset_vector, and combined_receiver
secondary_outcomes: raw response, backend input/output tokens, and wall time
common error categories: malformed output, wrong length, local-prefix-only, incorrect elementwise shift, other arithmetic error
frozen_predictions: If offset_vector exactness is high but combined_receiver exactness is low, composing prefix accumulation and shifting is a receiver execution bottleneck.
If offset_vector exactness remains low even with the prefix vector supplied, arithmetic application/output is an independent bottleneck and communication-format comparisons remain premature.

If all direct arithmetic conditions are high while simulator receivers fail, the dominant gap is more likely interaction/task orchestration; this inference remains limited to the tested harness and models.
analysis: Report exact counts and denominators per length/condition/model. Require the full raw response to parse as a JSON list of non-boolean integers; do not extract embedded arrays from prose. No significance test is planned for 8 cases per length.
limits: reused task inputs; this is a diagnostic ladder, not new held-out generalization evidence
direct single-agent completions differ from the multi-agent simulator prompt and context
one greedy run per input; no decoding variance estimate
checkpoint, scale, tokenizer, quantization and training differ together
only one arithmetic task family; no protocol or language comparison
